lesson_title: One Late Learner Broke the Average
hook_text: Nine friends averaged 19 minutes of homework. Then one person walked in — and the average said nobody was normal.
clip_script: Nine learners logged their homework minutes: 12, 14, 15, 15, 18, 21, 23, 25, 28. Share the total out equally and everyone gets 19 minutes — a fair, honest average. Then a tenth learner arrives: 120 minutes. Two full hours. Watch the average: the pot jumps to 291 minutes, and shared among ten that is 29,1 — but nine of the ten people did LESS than that. The average now describes almost nobody. One extreme value dragged it. Now watch the median: line everyone up in order and point at the middle — it barely moves, from 18 to 19,5, because the line does not care how extreme the last person is. That is the whole secret of statistics questions: outliers wreck the pot but never the line. When a monster value walks into the data, report the median — and say why.
visual_style: Animated queue of learners with floating minute-counters, a giant pot filling and overflowing when the 120 arrives, the mean marker lurching right while the median marker stays calmly in the middle of the line.
pacing: Calm setup, dramatic beat when the 120 lands, quick side-by-side of the lurching mean versus the steady median, crisp final rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master mean, median and mode.
